findings.scenario: Criterion IMP-066-073 requires reduced-motion and lifecycle safety as part of the typed motion contract. The persisted schema accepts any allowed kind/trigger/replay (including load+repeat and large x/y/rotation) with no reduced-motion policy, degrade mode, or never-hide invariant, and nothing in siteMotion.test.ts exercises prefers-reduced-motion. A player that faithfully runs the manifest will keep animating for reduced-motion users; entrance/hover opacity 0 can still hide content when JS only half-applies. Exit-is-manual is the only related guard.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit schema-level reduced-motion contract (e.g. required policy skip|opacity-only, forbid repeat/large translation unless skip, keep content visible without JS) and assert it in parse + persist tests.

findings.scenario: Breakpoint is a first-class field (all|mobile|tablet|desktop) but identity for apply/replace/remove is only (editId, kind). Applying entrance/mobile then entrance/desktop silently replaces the first entry, so distinct responsive variants cannot be persisted and last write wins.
findings.remediation: Include breakpoint in the replace/remove key (and unique-identity refine), or drop breakpoint from the schema if only one config per kind is allowed.

findings.scenario: Unique identity is enforced only on entry.id. A manifest with two different UUIDs and the same editId+kind parses successfully. inspectSiteMotion then returns duplicates; a later apply updates only the first match and leaves the other.
findings.remediation: Reject duplicate (editId, kind[, breakpoint]) in MotionManifestSchema and add a test that the composite key is unique.

findings.scenario: mutateSiteMotion writes site/motion-manifest.js via manifestScript(), which is the no-arbitrary-JS sink, but no test reads that file or checks </script> escaping. A regression that interpolates unsanitized JSON would still pass.
findings.remediation: After apply, read motion-manifest.js and assert it is only the escaped JSON assignment.

findings.scenario: availableEditIds is every data-edit-id, including canvas/iframe owners that assertMotionTarget rejects. Callers can present WebGL nodes as motion-editable and only fail on mutate.
findings.remediation: Filter availableEditIds with the same WebGL/iframe ownership rule as assertMotionTarget.

audit.proof_assessment: Proof artifacts are empty; only test source is available. Those tests do evidence constrained Zod kinds, rejection of selector/onComplete/unknown props/out-of-range values, apply-replace-remove-revert, one timeline per target, WebGL/unknown target rejection, blocking-gate rollback, and serialized concurrent applies. They do not evidence reduced-motion, composite unique identity, breakpoint variants, stable ids on replace, or the generated JS manifest.
residual_risks: Correctness of locking, snapshots, and gate rollback is entirely delegated to runGuardedMutation (not in this slice).
inspectSiteMotion is unlocked and can observe torn manifest/history/html.
History cursor is not bounded to entries.length; a hand-edited cursor can throw on revert.
MotionManifestSchema.parse / MotionEntrySchema.parse throw raw ZodError once past parseDraft.
Player-side listener/observer teardown is out of this module; schema gaps make unsafe playback more likely.
